event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: TYL’s 2023 filing squarely acknowledges COVID-19 as a continuing, enterprise-level threat even three years after the WHO declaration.  Risks are portrayed as both realised (e.g., prior supply-chain disruptions, one-off pandemic-related revenues that have now ceased) and prospective (possible new waves that could trigger renewed shutdowns, budget constraints, delayed procurements, and project slow-downs).  Although no dollar amount of foregone revenue is quantified, management explicitly warns of negative effects on fiscal-year-2023 performance, emphasises exposure to public-sector budget cycles, and cites concrete operational pinch-points such as hardware shortages, travel restrictions, implementation delays, and stretched receivables.  Mitigations are mentioned (remote-delivery capability, high proportion of recurring revenue), but these are framed as partial offsets rather than full risk neutralisers.  Given the filing date (Feb-2023) falls within three years of the pandemic onset, the Time Decay Principle permits high scores; however, because impacts are largely qualitative and not yet shown as material impairments, the evidence is assessed in the upper-mid range (scores 5-8).

evidence_list.snippet: COVID-19 may adversely affect our business and results of operations.

components.reason: Explicit statement that the pandemic can harm business and operations.
Applies in the present/future tense (ongoing risk).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Clear, direct warning of adverse impact with no mitigation or quantification yields a solid but not maximum risk score.

evidence_list.snippet: We expect that the continued global presence of COVID-19 may negatively impact our business and financial results in fiscal year 2023.

components.reason: Projects negative impact into the next fiscal year, signalling immediacy.
Connects pandemic to overall business and financial results.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Forward-looking language ties the pandemic to near-term financial performance, warranting a high risk rating.

evidence_list.snippet: As the virus continues to persist, increased infection rates (generally or as the result of new strains of the virus) may result in government authorities returning to stricter measures to contain the virus, including travel bans and restrictions, quarantines, and business limitations and shutdowns.

components.reason: Details concrete governmental responses (travel bans, shutdowns) that could disrupt operations.
Highlights potential worsening through new strains—escalation factor.
Forward-looking conditional wording indicates uncertainty, not certainty.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific operational restrictions are identified, but conditional language keeps score moderate-high.

evidence_list.snippet: While we are unable to accurately predict the full impact that COVID-19 will continue to have on our results from operations, financial condition, liquidity and cash flows due to numerous uncertainties, including the duration and severity of the pandemic and containment measures and associated compliance, the pandemic may negatively impact our revenues and other financial results.

components.reason: Links pandemic to results, liquidity and cash flows—broad financial scope.
Acknowledges uncertainty and inability to forecast precisely (adds risk).
Lacks quantification, slightly dampening severity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Broad but unquantified financial exposure keeps score in the middle of the allowable range.

evidence_list.snippet: Because an increasing portion of our revenues are recurring, the effect of COVID-19 on our results of operations may also not be fully reflected for some time.

components.reason: Indicates lagged recognition of pandemic impact, extending risk horizon.
Highlights high recurring revenue as a cushion (mitigation).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Lag effect adds modest concern but is fully offset by explicit mitigating factor, producing a neutral score.

evidence_list.snippet: We may see some more immediate impact on our business should there be new delays in government procurement processes and uncertainty around public sector budgets, or new delays in implementations caused by travel restrictions, closed offices, or clients shifting focus to more pressing issues.

components.reason: Specifies procurement and implementation delays tied to pandemic conditions.
Targets core client base (public sector), heightening exposure.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Concrete operational choke-points raise risk, but absence of hard numbers keeps score mid-high.

evidence_list.snippet: Appraisal and software implementations projects may be delayed if clients put projects on hold or slow projects by extending go-live dates.

components.reason: Directly links pandemic-driven client behaviour (project holds) to revenue-generating activities.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific operational delay noted; no magnitude or timeframe means a moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: While we have the ability to deliver most of our professional services remotely, some of our professional services, including appraisal assessments, are more effective when performed on-site, and certain clients may continue to insist on on-site services in any event.

components.reason: Shows partial mitigation via remote delivery.
Admits on-site dependence for key services, sustaining risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Risk and mitigation cancel out, leading to a neutral score.

evidence_list.snippet: There may be a negative impact on our revenues if we are unable to deliver these services.

components.reason: Explicitly ties service delivery challenges to revenue loss.
Conditional phrasing indicates potential, not definite impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Revenue risk is clear but still contingent, producing a moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: Also, we expect software licenses and subscriptions revenues to be negatively affected if there are delays in procurement processes.

components.reason: Predicts direct revenue decline in core lines (licenses, subscriptions).
Contingent on procurement delays—conditional wording.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Potential revenue hit to primary products merits a mid-high score.

evidence_list.snippet: Some clients could request changes to payment terms, negatively impacting the timing of collections of accounts receivables in future periods.

components.reason: Highlights cash-flow risk via slower collections.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Identifies liquidity pressure point, but without size or certainty, so moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: The ongoing COVID-19 pandemic has disrupted and may continue to disrupt the supply chain of hardware needed to maintain these third-party systems or to run our business.

components.reason: Describes actual supply-chain disruption already experienced.
Extends risk into the future with 'may continue to disrupt'.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Past and prospective supply-chain impacts elevate risk to upper-mid level.

evidence_list.snippet: A global economic slowdown, the COVID-19 pandemic, or similar circumstances could also adversely affect the businesses of our third-party providers, hindering their ability to provide the services on which we rely.

components.reason: Links pandemic to vendor performance, creating indirect operational risk.
Frames risk as conditional, not certain.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Vendor-dependency element adds risk, but conditional nature tempers score.

evidence_list.snippet: We presently consider the following to be among the important factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from our expectations and beliefs: (1) the continuing effects of the COVID-19 pandemic, including its potential effects on the economic environment, our customers and our operations, as well as any changes to federal, state or local government laws, regulations or orders in connection with the pandemic;

components.reason: Lists COVID-19 as a material risk factor affecting operations and economic environment.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Designation as a top material factor merits moderate risk score.

evidence_list.snippet: For the twelve months ended December 31, 2022, total revenues include COVID-related subscriptions revenue of $10.8 million from NIC’s Tour Health offering and professional services revenue of $40.2 million from pandemic unemployment and Virginia rent relief offerings.

components.reason: Provides quantified COVID-related revenue streams, showing exposure to volatile demand.
Positive revenue effect (benefit rather than loss) mitigates overall risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Quantification strengthens relevance but the revenue is favourable, so net risk moderate.

evidence_list.snippet: These programs all ended in 2022 and we do not expect to generate COVID-related subscriptions revenue and professional services revenue in future periods.

components.reason: Indicates loss of pandemic-specific revenue streams, revealing potential revenue gap.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Cessation of one-off revenues introduces downside but no scale given, keeping score moderate.
